meta.title: Project shader
meta.description: Colors each project in the left workspace sidebar and the sessions under it: a vertical "|" bar on the project row, a left-to-right color wash over its folder icon, and a tinted folder glyph; each session under it carries a lighter wash in the same color. Sliders double as switches: wash intensity 0 turns the gradient off and 100% fills the whole row with solid color (text auto-contrasts for readability); bar width 0 hides the bar; double-click any slider to restore its default. A fluorescent glow built on the perceptually uniform OKLCH space can apply on the light theme, the dark theme, or both (default dark only) — grays only brighten, never shift hue — with intensity 0 switching it off entirely. Session status markers light up the sidebar: a breathing halo while a session runs, a warning edge while it awaits input, a green edge for unread completions, each individually switchable; when a project is folded its session rows are unmounted, so the folded project row mirrors the strongest hidden status (such as the breathing halo) until the group expands again — separately switchable. Also included: ten one-click presets, a sticky live preview strip with a selectable sample color that shows every state at once (plain, running, awaiting input, unread, archived) and stays pinned while scrolling, collapsible settings sections that remember their fold, a Color-friendly mode (Okabe–Ito palette, doubled bars, textured washes), follow-the-theme brand colors, a per-project emphasis star, project search, a right-click "shuffle a color" item, 📌 multi-pin ordering (pinned groups move to the top with a color ring, ↑ ↓ sets the importance ranking; with nothing pinned the feature simply does nothing), a pulse-strength slider, and settings export/import as JSON. A "Project shader" entry in the sidebar's bottom icon column opens the settings panel; colors can also be switched from a project header's right-click menu ("Project color"). Choices live in this browser's local storage only: nothing leaves the device, clearing site data resets everything to defaults, and settings do not sync across devices or browsers. While enabled, the tinted folder glyph takes the place of the row's "contains the open session" highlight. Disabling or removing the plugin restores the plain sidebar.
